faq.q: How is WPM calculated?

seo.h2: What is a good WPM score?
p: An average computer user types about 40 WPM. Around 60 WPM is solid for most office and writing work. If you are just starting, do not chase speed — aim for above 95 percent accuracy first and your speed will rise on its own.

CPM means characters per minute. Some sites show CPM instead of WPM. Because one word equals five characters, you can convert easily: WPM = CPM / 5. This test shows you both numbers on the result panel so you can compare with any other typing test.

faq.q: What is a typing test?
faq.a: A typing test measures how fast and accurately you type. You type a passage of text while the test counts your words per minute (WPM), accuracy and errors.

faq.q: How is WPM calculated?
faq.a: WPM = (correct characters ÷ 5) ÷ minutes elapsed. The industry standard treats every 5 characters as one word, so longer words count more. Raw WPM ignores errors, while net WPM subtracts them.

faq.q: How long should a typing test be?
faq.a: 1 minute is the most popular length and is enough for a quick check. Longer tests (3, 5 or 10 minutes) give a more stable result because they average out short bursts of speed and fatigue.
